frame: metres, origin on the ground under the middle unless the kind's notes say otherwise, Blender -Y is the front, Z up; seats [x, y, z, yaw]: yaw = degrees of the sitter's facing, counter-clockwise seen from above, 0 = toward the object's front (-Y); size and bounds are in Blender axes (x, y, z)
asset_names: SM_South_<Kind>[_V<n>] (_V only for kinds with several variants)
atlas: M_North_Atlas (the North's, blender/north/gen); text slots M_South_Text_<id> from textures/localized/<lang>/south_<id>.png

meshes.notes: the «Маяк» lighthouse for the cliff top: a whitewashed round masonry tower tapering from r 2.30 (z 0.9) to r 1.55 (z 19.2) with two red bands (z 8.2..10.4 and 13.8..16.0), on a stone socle (r 2.42, to z 0.9) and a round concrete plinth r 3.1 (top z 0.3, bedded to z -0.5, nothing else under ground); three small windows up the shaft; a corbelled gallery (deck z 20.0, r 2.38) with a black rail (top z 21.06); a lantern room (drum to z 20.92, 12-sided opaque dark glazing z 20.92..22.50 with black bars), a black cap, a ball and a wind vane (top z 24.45). Origin on the ground under the tower's axis. Front (-Y): a plank door (0.9 x 2.0 m, closed, not enterable) between white jambs on the plinth and two steps off the plinth (treads z 0.2 and 0.1, out to y -3.8). A keeper's annex on +X (x 1.2..4.6, y +-1.5, flat concrete roof z 2.9, its door on -Y at x 3.8, windows on -Y and +X). Collision: box (collision_boxes, axis-aligned, mesh space): plinth, steps, door surround, annex, the tower as a stack of squares (side 1.8 r), gallery and lantern as two boxes. lamp = the lantern's centre (glazing is opaque: a future light needs it emissive or in front)

WW2 concrete pillbox half sunk into the cliff top: body 4.8 x 3.8 m (walls), roof slab 5.0 x 4.0 m, slab top z 1.6 (walkable roof), the body goes down to z -0.8 under ground. Front (-Y, toward the sea): a horizontal embrasure 1.4 x 0.3 m (z 0.68..0.98) splaying in to a dark back 0.6 m inside, a visor over it. Back (+Y): a doorway 0.9 x 1.1 m whose sill is at ground level, two steps down inside the wall (treads z -0.17, -0.34) to a dark liner 0.6 m in (not enterable), low wing walls either side (to y 2.80). The +X -Y corner is broken: the slab's corner is gone and the wall's edge chipped from z 0.4 up, rusty rebar stubs stick out, broken chunks lie at its foot (out to x 3.2, y -2.75). Damp dark band to z 0.35, lichen-grey roof with moss cushions. Collision: exact

the ribs and keel of an old wooden fishing boat half buried in beach sand, about 9 m long along X (stem at +X, curving up to z ~2.4 and leaning over to -Y; the sternpost at -X broken off at z ~0.8), beam ~3 m, heeled 11 degrees so the +Y side lies lower: 9 pairs of dark ribs of uneven height (five broken low, one gone), five strakes of grey planking left on the +Y side (partly running into the sand), a bit of gunwale on the high (-Y) side, a rusty strap, ring bolt on the stem. Origin on the sand under the middle; keel, rib feet and plank ends go down to z -0.5 (under the sand). No front (yaw freely). Collision: box (collision_boxes, mesh space; rot_x_deg right-handed about +X): the keel line (walkable along its top), the planked side as one tilted slab, the stem; nothing on the ribs, so one walks through between them

a big glacial erratic (a Baltic "Devil's stone"): rounded granite 4.5 x 3.5 m, top z 2.78, with a shallow hollow on top (near x 0.35, y 0.15) and a pale lichen crust on the front (-Y) shoulder; bedded 0.4 m (cut flat at z -0.4, nothing else under ground). Origin on the ground under the middle. No real front (the lichen side, -Y, reads best toward a path). Collision: exact

a split glacial erratic: one granite boulder (about 3.5 m across overall, 2.9 m deep, top z 2.23) cracked along a plane into two halves standing 1.0 m apart at the ground (the gap runs along Y through the origin), leaning a little away from each other: one can walk through. A lichen crust on the -X half's top. Bedded 0.4 m (cut flat at z -0.4). Origin on the ground in the middle of the gap. No front. Collision: exact (the gap stays open)
